description: The chart illustrates perplexity values for two measurement types—“Per-Output” and “Per-Layer”—across multiple sparsity rates, showing how the reported perplexity changes as the sparsity setting varies. The horizontal axis contains the categorical sparsity-rate levels labeled “10%,” “20%,” “30%,” “40%,” “50%,” “60%,” “70%,” and “80%,” arranged from left to right in increasing percentage order, and is labeled “Sparsity Rate.” The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks shown at powers of ten (e.g., around 10¹, 10², and 10³), spanning from single-digit perplexity values up to roughly 1000. For each sparsity category, there are two side-by-side bars: a blue bar for “Per-Output” and an orange bar for “Per-Layer,” as indicated by the legend in the upper-left of the plot. At 10% sparsity, both bars are just above 5 (approximately ~5–6); at 20% and 30% sparsity the bars remain in a similar single-digit range (roughly mid-5s to around ~6); at 40% and 50% sparsity the values increase slightly into the ~6–8 range; at 60% sparsity the blue bar is just under 10 and the orange bar is around ~10; at 70% sparsity the blue bar is around ~20 and the orange bar is around the mid-30s; and at 80% sparsity the blue bar rises to roughly ~500 while the orange bar is close to ~900, approaching the 10³ tick. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate with consistent coloring and no stacking, and there are no additional visual emphasis elements (such as outlines, annotations, or highlighted bars) beyond the legend and the logarithmic axis formatting.
